clue.text: Shows cargo in fine mess round mast

definitions.note: a description of the noun: the document that shows cargo

indicators.note: to mess round is to play about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Cargo lashed in a heap around a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: Shows looks like a verb, but the two words together describe a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's manifest is the official list of its cargo, presented to customs.

clue.text: Hesitate to go up to a flesheater

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Pausing before walking up to a carnivore.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a giant of folklore that eats human flesh.

clue.text: Up-to-date sailors follow one fashion

indicators.note: what follows is written after the other piece

parts.note: a mode is a fashion, one style among others

explanation.surface: Fashionable sailors all copy one particular look.
explanation.walkthrough: One adds nothing but the sense of a single style; it gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current, belonging to the present day.

clue.text: Sets aside a representative to go to jumble sale

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: jumbled things are mixed up, so the word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rep sent along to a jumble sale, a charity sale of second-hand goods, sorts things aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumble sale is one phrase in the surface; the first word is the instruction, the second the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke it, setting it aside.

clue.text: Girl in hat of superior knight

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a beret is a soft flat cap

explanation.surface: A girl wearing the hat of a high-ranking knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight banneret led men under his own banner and ranked above a knight bachelor.

clue.text: Climbing with difficulty, having to clasp girl in embrace

indicators.note: to clasp something is to hold it within one's arms

parts.note: to cling is to hold tight

explanation.surface: A struggling climber has to hold a girl close as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamber is to climb awkwardly using hands and feet.

clue.text: Submits to arbitrator with signs of hesitation

parts.note: er is a hesitant noise, here several

explanation.surface: Someone yields to the umpire's ruling with a few ums and ers.
explanation.walkthrough: Submits to arbitrator reads as one phrase; the definition is only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a matter is to submit it to someone else for a decision.

clue.text: Tree found in small wood on island

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing sitting on another is written after it

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: A walker spots a particular tree growing in a little island copse.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangrove is a tropical tree that grows in coastal swamps.

clue.text: They support everything that is successful at first

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Supporters always back whatever is winning at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are partners who back and help one another, so they are those who support.

clue.text: Splendid measure if brought back

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A dubious claim that some fine measure would be glorious if it were reintroduced.
explanation.walkthrough: EN, half an em, is a printing measure that crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine is a common adjective of approval meaning excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Two for example yet more insensible to feeling

parts.note: the comparative of numb, read as numb-er

explanation.surface: Someone even more emotionally deadened than before, with the number two thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The second word is not the noun for a figure but the comparative adjective, more numb; the definition then reads it as the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Two divides exactly by two, making it an instance of that class of integer.

clue.text: River always runs between two pearls

indicators.note: letters placed between two others sit inside the pair

parts.note: the text as filed reads pearls, which gives nothing; the letters needed are S and N, the two poles

explanation.surface: A river flowing for ever between two pearls.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text reads pearls, almost certainly a misreading of poles: S and N, south and north, must sit around the word for always. The Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is a named river flowing between Wales and England, so river is its category.

clue.text: He was an artist for two kings

wordplay.note: Edward, name of eight English kings, followed by Lear, Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A court painter who worked in turn for two monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: Kings here are names, not patrons: the artist's first and last names each belong to a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear, known for nonsense verse, was a professional landscape painter and gave drawing lessons to Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Bounty for a capital character, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the phrase, not its spelling

parts.note: a capital letter is a large one, and the letter here is S

explanation.surface: A reward offered for catching some notable figure in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like a city and character like a person; both are about lettering.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, a bounty or liberality bestowed on others.

clue.text: Servant may set out with drawback

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: split as draw back: the word draw, written back to front

explanation.surface: A servant might list a disadvantage of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawback reads as one word meaning a snag, but it splits into a word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is someone employed to manage a household or serve passengers, a kind of servant.

clue.text: Time to close the book and check back?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the reading is finished
second meaning: to look through something again to verify it

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the phrase into two words, reading done and finished; the second uses it as the ordinary verb for reviewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Once the reading is over you shut the book, and to read something over is to go back and check it.

clue.text: Colourful composer?

parts.note: surface reading: a composer whose music is vivid and lively
setter's reading: a composer whose surname is also the word for one who colours things

explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Stainer was a Victorian English composer of church music, best known for The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stainer is someone who applies colour or dye, and Stainer is also the composer's name.

clue.text: They prevent one hearing damage done to pear by slug, perhaps

indicators.note: damaged things are broken up and their parts put back differently

explanation.surface: A gardener complains of a slug eating the pears, a scene with nothing to do with hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earplugs are worn in the ears to block sound.

clue.text: Can't stand the boy in the river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Test is a Hampshire trout river

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the lad who keeps splashing about in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's in runs loosely: the river goes inside the boy's name, not the other way round. The Test is a river in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to hate it, to be unable to bear or stand it.

clue.text: Light match and present easy target

parts.note: light in colour, as fair hair or skin

explanation.surface: Striking a match makes a smoker an easy target for a sniper.
explanation.walkthrough: Light and match pair up as fire-lighting words; each is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair game is a person or thing that may legitimately be attacked or mocked, a ready target.

clue.text: Entertained Medusa unawares

indicators.note: caught unawares, the word is thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The Gorgon Medusa was hosted by someone who did not know who she was.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused means pleasantly occupied or diverted, as an entertained audience is.

clue.text: Look for fish with colour on the outside

indicators.note: something on the outside wraps around whatever it covers

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Search for a brightly coloured fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Look for reads as one phrasal verb, but the definition is just Look and for joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it, and a regard is also a look or gaze.

clue.text: A woman having something to eat after foreign royalty

indicators.note: coming after means written to the right of the other piece

parts.note: a ras is an Ethiopian prince or ruler

explanation.surface: A woman sits down to a meal served after the visiting royals.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle of the clue, unusually: the woman, having come after the royalty, gives the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin slice of bacon or ham, food for the breakfast plate.

clue.text: Flower arrangement plus complete authority

indicators.note: an arrangement sets the letters out in a new order

explanation.surface: A florist given a free hand over the display.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrangement belongs with flower in the surface, but here it works on both words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Full powers is the term for total delegated authority, as given to an ambassador or envoy.

clue.text: Head of the voting

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an election or count of votes

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the person at the top of an election; the two nouns are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Poll survives as an archaic word for the human head, and it also names the casting of votes.

clue.text: It may be worked into a story

definitions.text: It may be worked into a story

parts.words: It may be worked into a story
parts.note: surface reading: some detail a writer weaves into a tale
setter's reading: worked also suggests land that is dug, the other sense of the same short word

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as being about writing, but worked hints at a piece of ground that is cultivated.
explanation.definitionFit: Every narrative is built around its plot, and a plot is also a small patch of land that gets worked.

clue.text: Gratify royal point

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Pleasing a monarch over some detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to delight or entertain them, as with stories or a feast.

clue.text: Flower found in glove returned in tattered hat

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the word runs backwards
whatever is found in something lies inside it, and the clue repeats the idea with its second in
a tattered thing is torn about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A flower tucked inside a glove inside a battered old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower here is a thing that flows, a river; the Volga is Europe's longest, in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower for a river because a river flows; the Volga is one.
